newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus sees lower Polish inflation.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus sees lower Polish inflation.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus voiced optimism on Thursday that Poland can reduce inflation to west European levels by the end of the century.
"I am sure that Poland can have legitimately that ambition," the head of the International Monetary Fund told a news conference.

He said that Poland has had "enormous success" in managing its economy but acknowledged that the country has had problems reducing inflation from about 20 percent -- difficulties that it is not alone in encountering.
Camdessus called wage indexation one of the key obstacles facing Poland in its anti-inflation drive.
But he voiced confidence in the resolve of the Polish authorities to tackle inflation, provided they have the needed support of the country's parliament.
